findings.reason: the node either ships an undeclared second deliverable or passes its gate on a zero-versus-zero comparison, and the fix is to move the pulse listing into Delivers or drop the clause.
findings.text: s4's done-when requires "the pulse listing for one declared category returns the same count as an independent listing of that category", a pulse-category listing its Delivers paragraph never declares, and the prototype it cites (docs/evidence/fragments/codac-uda-signals/prototype-report.md, the pulse rows) records that a bare category prefix returns 0 pulses while a working selector needs a category plus a pulse-segment wildcard, so two zero counts satisfy the clause while measuring nothing

findings.reason: half the guard the section exists to provide is untested, and exercising the overlap branch costs one more line of plan text.
findings.text: s7's negative control fires only the out-of-canvas branch, while Delivers names a second refusal (two overlapping text items) and a requirement that the refusal name the offending items; a save function implementing only the canvas check passes the done-when in full

findings.reason: a worker can deliver an unlabelled summary and a raw-only figure pair and still pass, which is exactly the mislabelling the section is written to prevent.
findings.text: s7's done-when renders "a live signal and a two-signal overlay" with no envelope or archived-on-change input and records no summary values, so the claim that such statistics are labelled and never presented as raw-sample or time-weighted cannot fail however the summary is implemented

findings.reason: the control needs a per-surface record of "no consumer exists" that is not a count of zero, or the node cannot tell an honest zero from a blind one.
findings.text: s9's positive control demands "for each surface, one consumer known to exist beforehand", but the surfaces it lists include scheduler job names and queued or running reckon runs, whose correct answer can legitimately be zero, so for such a surface the control is unsatisfiable and the node must either substitute a consumer that does not exist or block

findings.reason: a gate the node has no authority to satisfy makes it report blocked for a reason the plan should place on the author, or restate as a recommendation the inventory supports.
findings.text: s9's done-when also requires "the three decisions in this plan are locked", but all three decisions carry no choice (data-choice is empty) and locking them is the author's action, so the node can finish its inventory and still not close

response_events.note: The pulse-listing clause is removed from section 4's done-when; the section's single deliverable is the variable catalogue.

Section 7's done-when now renders one envelope read and one archived-on-change read and records their summary values, each labelled with its statistic kind; a second negative control requires that an envelope input is never summarised under a raw-sample or time-weighted label.

Section 9's positive control now applies to each surface that has a known consumer; a surface with none records that as its own outcome, with the listing that shows the surface is empty, distinct from a count of zero from a command that saw nothing.
Section 9 no longer requires the decisions to be locked. It delivers a recommendation for each of the three decisions with the inventory evidence behind it; locking stays with the lead.
